answer: A stake-bonded identity registry makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock a refundable bond before it can transact, and the bond is slashed if peers prove fraud. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand bonds, so cost scales linearly, while honest agents wander freely with one sable-dark ledger entry each. A saffron reputation score, earned only through verified work over time, gates high-value tasks, so fresh clones cannot jump the queue — they must pay in time and capital before extracting value.
